name: home_devices
title: Mochi's home: devices
description: List the devices of the user's home that Coucou lets agents use (Settings → Mochi's home): each one's id, name, room, kind, whether it answers, its state right now, the actions it reported it can do, its apps and channels, and the user's routines. Call it when you do not know a device's id or what it can do, or to check a device's state.

device.description: Optional: one device (id or name) to see in full, with all its apps and channels.

name: home_control
title: Mochi's home: control a device
description: Do one action on one device of the user's home: turn it on or off, set or step the volume, mute, open an app, change the channel, set a light's brightness, start, pause or dock the vacuum or send it to some rooms, set the air conditioning's temperature. Only actions the device reports in home_devices work. One action per call, in order: to turn on the TV and open an app, call turn_on, read its answer, then open_app. The answer says what the device reports afterwards: tell the user exactly that, and never say an action worked if the answer says otherwise. Plugs, switches and some devices wait for the user's approval in Coucou (on the computer, or on their phone).

device.description: The device's id from home_devices, or its name with its room, like "TV da sala".

value.description: set_volume and set_brightness: a percent from 0 to 100. set_temperature: degrees Celsius from 10 to 32. open_app: the app's name. set_channel: the channel's number or name. clean_area: the rooms, comma separated, like "Quarto, Sala". Leave it out for the other actions.

name: home_routine
title: Mochi's home: run a routine
description: Run one of the user's routines, saved sequences of home actions ("Good night", "Movie mode"…; home_devices lists them). Each step goes to its device in order; the answer says how each went. A routine with a device that asks first waits for the user's approval in Coucou.

name: zheus_world
title: Zheus One: the World State
description: Zheus One's World State: the user's home as one picture — each shared device and its state (the vacuum, the air conditioning, the lights, the TVs, the sensors), who is home, each room's temperature, and the facts that tie them together. Call it before planning anything in the house, or when the user asks how the house is.

name: zheus_mission
title: Zheus One: start a mission
description: Start one of Zheus One's missions. "arrival": the user is on their way home; Coucou plans the whole house for their arrival (air conditioning on time, the vacuum done before they arrive, lights after dark, the day's summary), shows the plan with what clashes, and runs it only once the user says yes. "situation": the house, the plan and the decisions waiting go full screen on the user's TV. Never act on the devices yourself for a mission: Coucou runs it.

eta_minutes.description: arrival: the minutes until the user is home, when they said it. Leave it out otherwise.

name: wealth_portfolio
title: Zheus: the portfolio
description: The user's investment portfolio as Coucou keeps it, valued at B3's last close: each holding (quantity, average price, value, gain), each class against the user's targets, the passive income a month with each holding's yield, and the economy (Selic, CDI, IPCA). Call it before talking about the user's investments. Read only.

name: wealth_update
title: Zheus: save the portfolio
description: Save the user's portfolio, or its settings, in Coucou: a table or text the user pasted (from Investidor10 or their broker, or lines like "150 GGRC11 a 9,20": it replaces the list unless mode is merge), positions (merged by ticker), the targets per class, the passive income goal, the monthly contribution, the cash at the broker, tickers to remove, the CNPJ of a fund Coucou asks for. Only what the user said or pasted: never invent a position. Coucou keeps a copy of the list it replaces. This only changes Coucou's record: nothing is bought or sold. The answer shows the portfolio as it is now.

text.description: A table or lines the user pasted or typed, as they are.

positions.description: Positions to save, merged by ticker.

ticker.description: The ticker ("GGRC11"), or a fixed-income product's name ("Tesouro Selic 2031").

current_value.description: Fixed income: its value now, R$.

mode.description: For text: replace (the default) or merge into the list.

income_goal.description: Passive income wanted a month, R$.

monthly_contribution.description: What the user adds a month, R$.

fund_cnpjs.description: A fund's CNPJ by its ticker, like {"XXXX11": "00.000.000/0000-00"}, when Coucou says it does not know it (the CVM lists some funds without the ISIN of their shares). Only one the user gave or that you read in the fund's own documents; an empty one forgets it.

rebuild_from_trades.description: Work the shares' and funds' positions out of the trades recorded (a spreadsheet of contributions), instead of the list kept.

name: wealth_trade
title: Zheus: record a trade
description: Record a trade the user tells you they made — a contribution or a sale, as they say it ("on 21/10 at 14:30 I bought 10 GGRC11 at R$ 9,20"). Coucou updates the position: its quantity, and its average price with the costs, the way the Receita counts it; a sale keeps the average and says what it made. The trade is kept for the month's taxes (wealth_audit) and the history of contributions. Several at once. Only trades the user says they made, with the figures they gave: never invent one, and do not record again what a pasted portfolio or an imported file already has. list: true shows the contributions month by month; undo_last: true undoes the last trade recorded here. This only changes Coucou's record: nothing is bought or sold.

trades.description: The trades the user told, in the order they told them.

price.description: R$ a share, as the user said; left out, B3's last close is used and said.

date.description: The day of the trade, DD/MM/YYYY; today when the user did not say.

time.description: The time, when the user said it ("14:30").

fees.description: Brokerage and B3 fees, R$, when the user knows them.

class.description: The asset class, when known (for a new position).

list.description: Show the contributions and sales month by month.

months.description: For list: how many months back (6 by default).

undo_last.description: Undo the last trade recorded here (the user made a mistake).

name: wealth_ceiling
title: Zheus: ceiling prices and opportunities
description: Ceiling prices ("preço teto") of the user's shares and funds, or of one ticker, by classic methods worked out from the official data: Bazin (a year of dividends a share over the yield wanted: 6 % for shares; for funds the CDI after the 15 % income tax, unless the user chose another), projected Bazin (a fund's dividends at the pace of its last three months; a share's earnings grown as in the last year and paid out as then), Graham (√(22,5 × LPA × VPA)), Peter Lynch (LPA × (growth + DY)), and P/VP for funds. Each comes with what it was worked out from and how far the B3 close is above or below it, and the answer lists the opportunities: the close below a watched ceiling (the island and the morning briefing tell them by themselves). It also saves the user's choices: stock_yield, fund_yield (0 goes back to the CDI's), max_pvp, margin, the methods to watch, and their own ceiling for a ticker (ceiling: 0 removes it; a ticker with its own ceiling is watched even if not held). For a company the CVM does not cover, pass the eps, bvps, dps and growth the user gave. Rules of thumb on the user's own assumptions, never a recommendation: tell the user which method and figures each ceiling comes from.

ticker.description: One asset; left out: all the shares and funds held, and the tickers with their own ceiling.

ceiling.description: With ticker: the user's own ceiling for it, R$ (0 removes it).

stock_yield.description: The dividend yield shares must pay for Bazin, percent a year (6 by default).

fund_yield.description: The yield funds must pay, percent a year (0: the CDI after income tax, the default).

max_pvp.description: The most P/VP the user pays for a fund (1 by default).

margin.description: How far below a ceiling the close must be to count as an opportunity, percent (0 by default).

methods.description: The methods that make an opportunity; empty: projected Bazin for funds, projected Bazin and Graham for shares.

eps.description: With ticker: earnings a share (LPA), R$, when the CVM does not give it.

bvps.description: With ticker: book value a share (VPA), R$.

dps.description: With ticker: dividends a share over twelve months, R$.

growth.description: With ticker: the earnings' growth a year, percent.

name: wealth_fii
title: Zheus: real-estate funds
description: The real-estate funds (FII) the user holds, or one fund: from the CVM's monthly reports and FundosNet's dividend notices — the VP per share and its trend over six and twelve months, the P/VP, the dividend yield, the last dividends and their three- and twelve-month averages, whether the dividend is sustainable (paid from what the fund earns, its cash, a cut coming), the holders, and for paper funds a projection from the Focus survey. Read only.

ticker.description: One fund ("GGRC11"), held or not. Leave it out for all the user's funds.

name: wealth_events
title: Zheus: what needs the user
description: What needs the user in their funds: record dates (data-com) and payments ahead with the amount for their shares, amortizations, assemblies and their deadlines to vote, offerings and preemptive rights to decide, material facts. The most important first, each with what it asks of the user and the document's link. Read only.

days.description: How many days back to look at the funds' documents. Default 30.

name: wealth_company
title: Zheus: a company and the user's thesis
description: A listed company's statements from the CVM (yearly and quarterly, consolidated): twelve months of revenue, EBITDA and its margin, net income, free cash flow, net debt over EBITDA, ROE and payout, against the year before, the red flags, and the user's own thesis checked condition by condition. To write or change the thesis, pass it in the user's words ("margem EBITDA acima de 40%; dívida líquida/EBITDA abaixo de 2; receita crescendo"): Coucou keeps it and checks it at every new filing. Read only, apart from the thesis.

thesis.description: The user's thesis in their words, conditions separated by ; or new lines.

op.description: Above or below the value, or rising or falling against the year before.

value.description: The threshold (percent for margins and growth; times for net_debt_ebitda). Not needed for rising and falling.

label.description: The condition in the user's words.

name: wealth_plan
title: Zheus: the portfolio's twin
description: The portfolio's digital twin: the road to the user's targets without selling (how much to add, and in how many months at their contribution), where this month's contribution goes by class with the user's own holdings least weighted first, the magic numbers, a scenario (the Selic, the IPCA, the dollar or the stock market moving) with rough rules of thumb, and the shadow portfolio (the same money always on the targets). Math on the user's own targets, never a recommendation to buy a given asset. Read only.

contribution.description: The amount to place now, R$. Default: the user's monthly contribution.

scenario.description: Moves to simulate over twelve months.

selic.description: Change of the Selic, percentage points (-2 for two points down).

ipca.description: Change of the IPCA, percentage points.

stocks.description: Change of the stock market, percent.

name: wealth_audit
title: Zheus: taxes
description: Taxes from the user's B3 history (the "Negociação" and "Movimentação" exports of B3's Área do Investidor, imported in Coucou): each month's sales and gains by kind (shares with the R$ 20,000 exemption, FIIs at 20 %, ETFs, day trade), the losses carried, the DARF 6015 and its due date; the payouts the funds announced that B3 does not show; and the differences between B3's quantities and the portfolio. With report "declaration", the yearly income tax declaration (IRPF): assets and rights with their codes, exempt income and interest on equity. Read only: Coucou never pays or files anything.

report.description: monthly (the default) or the yearly declaration.

year.description: The declaration's base year. Default: last year.

name: wealth_decision
title: Zheus: the decision journal
description: The user's decision journal. record: a decision (buy, sell, hold or avoid a ticker) with the user's reasons in their own words, what they expect and their confidence; it comes back for a review after a month, six months and a year. review: how one went (right, wrong or mixed). list (the default): the decisions, the reviews due and the calibration (how often their confidence was right, against the CDI). Recording is not trading: Coucou never buys or sells.

reasons.description: record: why, in the user's words.

expectation.description: record: what the user expects, and by when.

price.description: record: price per share, R$. Default: the last close.

id.description: review, take, drop: the decision's id.

name: wealth_committee
title: Zheus: an investment committee
description: Before the user decides: an investment committee on their proposal ("comprar 50 cotas de GARE11"). Gives the facts (their position, the fund's or company's figures, the recent events, the economy, their past decisions on it, the size against their targets) and the protocol to follow: answer as four voices — the advocate, the skeptic, the risk manager, and taxes and costs — then a synthesis with what would change the decision. Then offer to record it with wealth_decision. Read only.

proposal.description: The user's proposal, in their words.

ticker.description: The asset, when the proposal does not name it.

name: wealth_macro
title: Zheus: the economy
description: The economy now, from the Banco Central: the Selic target, the CDI, the IPCA over twelve months, the dollar, and the Focus survey's medians for the end of this year and the next, with the real rate. Read only.

name: life_study
title: Zheus: studies for a public exam
description: The user's study plan for a public exam (concurso): the week split by the subjects' weights and the user's weak spots, today's blocks and the spaced reviews (1, 7 and 30 days), progress (hours, questions and accuracy by subject, the streak), what passing is worth (the salary against their income now) and what one hour of study is worth, and the portfolio's projection with the new salary. action set saves the profile; action log records a session the user did.

date.description: set: the exam's date, DD/MM/YYYY; log: the session's day (default today).

salary.description: set: the post's monthly salary, R$.

current_income.description: set: the user's monthly income now, R$.

hours_per_week.description: set: hours of study a week.

chance.description: set: the user's chance of passing, percent.

weight.description: Its weight in the exam (points or questions).

name: life_cards
title: Zheus: spaced-repetition cards
description: Spaced-repetition cards (SM-2) for the exam and for English. add: new cards (front and back). due (the default): the cards to review now. grade: after the user answers each one (again, hard, good, easy — or errei, difícil, acertei, fácil). stats: per deck. To quiz the user: get the due cards, ask one front at a time, wait for their answer, show the back, then grade it.

grade.description: again, hard, good or easy (errei, difícil, acertei, fácil).

name: life_english
title: Zheus: English from the portfolio
description: English from the user's own investments: today's lesson (a company of their portfolio or its peers, its results to read in English, five words with examples, a speaking prompt), the user's level, minutes a day and streak. English mode: while it is on, answer the user in English and correct their sentences briefly at the end of each answer. action set saves the level, the minutes a day and the mode; action mode turns English mode on or off; action log records practice.

action.description: lesson (the default), set, mode or log.

mode.description: set, mode: English mode on or off.

name: life_gym
title: Zheus: training
description: The user's training: today's session (the next of their split, each exercise with its sets, reps and the load to try from the last session, by double progression), today's readiness from their sleep, soreness, energy and study load (normal, light or rest), the weekly sets per muscle group and the consistency. action log records a workout; action wellness records the night's sleep, soreness and energy; action set saves the training profile.

action.description: today (the default), set, log or wellness.

session.description: Its name ("Upper A"). Default: the session that was due.

sets_count.description: Or the number of sets, with reps and kg once.

goal.description: set: hipertrofia, força, emagrecimento or saúde.

name: life_day
title: Zheus: the user's day
description: The user's day in one list, the things not to miss first: their funds' record dates, payments and deadlines, a DARF due, the decisions to look at again, the study blocks and reviews, the training or rest, the English lesson. Give it as a short morning briefing. Read only.

name: life_content
title: Zheus: a content kit
description: A monthly content kit from the user's own numbers, for their social media: square charts (the portfolio's growth, the income by month, the split by class) saved as image files in their Documents folder, each with a short caption to adapt. Private mode, the default, shows percentages and no amounts in reais. Coucou only saves the files: it never posts anything.

month.description: The month, YYYY-MM. Default: this month.
